info.title: Diagnostics
info.summary: Read-only views of the knowledge bases: where every source and reading came from.

get.description: The view's name, as `configs/app_config.json` holds it under `ui`.

Every work of every knowledge base served: the free catalog in its order, then the licensed works as their
export lists them. Only the free knowledge base has a catalog.

An HTML work (the operator's 6.a): its outline by heading and its sections, from the search index; where the index is
not built, the work says so and names the command.
One section of an HTML work as indexed, its chunks in order with where each stands in the section's text.

The article, chapter or other top unit that holds a section, whole: every section with its original and its
chunks, its dropped headings at their place, in the work's order.

One judgement of the page shown as it judged (181.a): its reading, read-only, with its findings on the blocks.
`judgement` is the id a page's judgement carries (`<reading key>:<version>:<again>`).

The text the search and the chat quote for the page. Where the export has not cut a book's quoted text on this
machine, the core cuts it on the first call, about a minute for a large one, and keeps it.
Every run of the pipeline, newest first, both knowledge bases together; a base not listed says why.
One run whole: its code version, its cost by provider, and the pages it chose a reading for.
The whole pipeline at a glance, each knowledge base beside the other; a base not served says why.
The pages behind a figure of the overview: every page served that matches every filter given.

Every work of both knowledge bases, how far it is converted and why pages did not pass, as the core counted it;
under --public-only the licensed shelf is never read.
The judge's and stage 2's findings grouped by kind, block class and work, void ones apart, with their pages.

Every version of the reader's and the judge's instructions (148.a): its state, its sha256 now and frozen, why it
was made, its text, and its change from the version before it.

The search server's call log, newest first: who asked what, which pages answered, how long it took. Under
--public-only only the calls that concern the free knowledge base alone, and how many were left out.
Whether the chat answers here, and its example questions.

post.description:
One turn of the chat, the one route here that spends money: the core's chat agent answers, the turn goes to
its conversation's log, and the turn comes back as the log keeps it, without the agent's own words.

get.description: The search the MCP server answers with, over the knowledge bases given out; "nothing found" is an answer.

Whether a person's verdict is taken here (the app started with --allow-verdicts), the lists its dialog offers in
the core's words, and each knowledge base's background export, which the view follows to reload a page.

post.description:
A person's verdict on the reading a page shows, the one route here that writes (213.b): recorded at once by the
core, append-only, and the export set going in the background. 403 when the app was started without
--allow-verdicts or the request comes from elsewhere; 422 with the core's sentence for an input it refuses.

A correction's text as the table it would be (204.a's path), for the dialog to show before it is sent; writes
nothing.

AnsweredWork.title: AnsweredWork
AnsweredWork.description: A work that answered a search over works (`search_works`, decision 124.a).

AppInfo.title: AppInfo
AppInfo.description:
The name the view shows in its header and its browser tab (decision 149.c): a working name, kept in the app's own
config so it changes in one place, without code.

ArticleLink.title: ArticleLink
ArticleLink.description: Where the diagnostics shows an HTML section the chat cites: its article, scrolled to the section (decision 164.a).

Attempt.title: Attempt
Attempt.description:
One reading ever bought for a page, as the export lists them, oldest first. Its text stays in the private store;
only the reading the page shows is exported, so the others are shown by their record alone.

AttemptCheck.title: AttemptCheck
AttemptCheck.description: What the check made of one reading: its state, the judge's verdict where it judged, and the check's outcome.

Block.title: Block
Block.description: One block of a reading, in the form the view draws it; which of the body fields is set depends on the class.

Chosen.title: Chosen
Chosen.description: Why the page's reading was chosen over its others, by which run and when (the pipeline database, 51.a).

ChosenPage.title: ChosenPage
ChosenPage.description: A page one run chose a reading for, and why.

ExportStatus.title: ExportStatus
ExportStatus.description:
The background export of one knowledge base: whether one runs or waits, how many have finished (a view reloads its
data when this number moves), and the last one's error, said rather than hidden.

HtmlArticle.title: HtmlArticle
HtmlArticle.description:
A top unit of a work's outline whole, on one scroll (the operator, 10 Nov: a click on "Sharpe ratio" should show the whole
article): a Wikipedia article, an SRE chapter, a chapter of Lefèvre. The section asked for is the one to scroll to.

HtmlArticleEntry.title: HtmlArticleEntry
HtmlArticleEntry.description:
One place in an article's scroll, in the work's order: a section with its original and its chunks, a heading the
loader dropped as noise with its original alone, or a heading with no text of its own, which stands as a heading.

HtmlChunk.title: HtmlChunk
HtmlChunk.description:
A chunk as the index embedded it, and where its text stands in its section's text: start and end as character
offsets, None where it is not found there. `overlap` is how many of its first characters the chunk before it shares.

HtmlNode.title: HtmlNode
HtmlNode.description: A heading of the work's outline. Its label is its own section's; a heading with no text of its own has none.

HtmlSectionRow.title: HtmlSectionRow
HtmlSectionRow.description: A section in the flat table, in the work's order.

Judge.title: Judge
Judge.description: Which judge judged the reading the page shows, and with which version of its prompt (147.a).

Judgement.title: Judgement
Judgement.description:
One judge's judgement of one reading (147.a), oldest first: by which version of the judge's prompt, in which state
that version is (a prototype, the active one, retired), whether the judge was asked again, and whether it counts.

ModelRow.title: ModelRow
ModelRow.description:
A model or a provider: the pages it worked on in each knowledge base and what all its work on them cost, retries
included. A cost is None where it did not work there, or where the export gives no cost.

OutlineUnit.title: OutlineUnit
OutlineUnit.description: One unit of a work's own order as the core cut it (decision 84.a), with its whole subtree's pages in figures.

Overview.title: Overview
Overview.description:
The overview in its bands (the operator's 18.a): the key figures, which model did what, the pages through the pipeline,
what the search holds; the latest runs stand with each base's key figures.

PageLink.title: PageLink
PageLink.description: Where the diagnostics shows a hit's page: the page view of an exported reading.

PageReset.title: PageReset
PageReset.description: A person's reset of a page (191.a): the reading discarded, the text layer served until a new reading is due.

PersonMark.title: PersonMark
PersonMark.description:
A person's standing verdict on the reading a page shows, beside the judge's state wherever a page's state stands
(decision 166.a): accepted or rejected by the latest accept or reject that applies, as the core decides what is served
(`served_readings.human_standing`); noted where only a note applies, which never changes what is served. Its reason
and note go in the hover.

PersonVerdict.title: PersonVerdict
PersonVerdict.description:
A person's verdict on a page or one of its blocks (146.a): accept, reject or a note, with the reason given. One
given on an earlier reading of the page does not apply to the one shown, and says so.

PromptPart.title: PromptPart
PromptPart.description: What a prompt file is, as the registry's `parts` names it: its key, its name before the colon, the rest after.

QuotedText.title: QuotedText
QuotedText.description:
The text the search and the chat quote for a page (decision 93.a), from the core's one function for it: the served
reading as quotable text, or the cleaned text layer where the reading is not served.

ReaderRule.title: ReaderRule
ReaderRule.description:
A rule a judge proposed for the reader (decisions 195.a, 197.a: judge/4), shown read-only beneath its judgement and
never applied (202.a): its kind (a format rule, a class or an attribute of the vocabulary), the block that asked for it,
the rule in the judge's words, and the class, attribute and value it names, where it names one. The export writes ''
for a field not set; here it is None.

ReadingError.title: ReadingError
ReadingError.description:
A validator error on the reading, parted into what it names (decision 228.a, the operator on accounting p. 398: "then the only thing that still confuses me is that the error stands at the top, although I entered a correction"): the block and the line, where it
names them, so the view marks the error on its block and opens the raw text at its line. `looked` is the verdict of
the latest person's verdict that applies to the block, else to the page as a whole (`looked_at`), and `corrected`
whether a person's correction stands for the block: the view then mutes the error and says so, never hides it, as the
error is the validator's verdict on the reading, which a person's verdict does not change.

Recalled.title: Recalled
Recalled.description:
One judgement shown on the page as it judged it (decision 181.a, the operator: "you see what the old judge looked like, applied to the page"): the reading it judged, read-only, its findings on that reading's blocks, and what is shown in
one line. Never the standing view, and the view marks it so.

RouteLevel.title: RouteLevel
RouteLevel.description:
A route level, what it means in the core's words (`served_readings.ROUTE_LEVELS`), and how many of the work's pages
are served at it: the routes' one line, and their legend.

RouteRow.title: RouteRow
RouteRow.description: One route a work's pages are served by, as a person reads the routes (the operator, 10 Nov: "is this route a faulty one?"): how good it is, where the text comes from, by which reader, why, and on how many pages.

RunLine.title: RunLine
RunLine.description: One run as a list shows it: what was run, when, how it ended, what it cost, the batches it sent.

SectionRow.title: SectionRow
SectionRow.description: One value of a section's field, with its count in each knowledge base; None where it does not occur there.

Segment.title: Segment
Segment.description:
A piece of prose as the core parsed it: text, math, code, or an inline mark of its own (decision 206.a): a note's
marker (`fn`, "[4]{.fn}"), a superscript (`sup`) or a subscript (`sub`). A marker names the footnote on the same page
whose `marker` is its content (`with_notes`), and carries that note's text, so the view links the two; both None where
the page has no such note.

Splitter.title: Splitter
Splitter.description:
How the index cuts a section into chunks, as `chunking.splitting_config` gives it: the view's legend of the overlap
says from it why a chunk repeats the end of the one before.

Stage2.title: Stage2
Stage2.description: Stage 2 of the check (146.a): the reading against the PDF's text layer, in figures and findings.

Stage2Finding.title: Stage2Finding
Stage2Finding.description: What stage 2 found comparing the reading with the PDF's text layer; an older plan gives the kind alone.

StandingCorrection.title: StandingCorrection
StandingCorrection.description:
The correction that stands for a block (decision 229.a, the operator: "what you really want to see first is the correction"): the
latest a person gave that applies to the reading shown, drawn first as the block's content, the reader's text muted
beneath it. Never served: the search and the chat quote the reading or the text layer, and the reading is unchanged.

StateCount.title: StateCount
StateCount.description:
A listed state's count, and how many of its pages a person's standing verdict accepted, rejected or noted (166.a:
"ok 399 · 1 accepted"; 211.a: "decided by a person 8 · 7 accepted · 1 noted"). `counted_states` sets them on every
count it makes; they are optional only so a count of an older shape still reads.

StatePages.title: StatePages
StatePages.description:
The pages behind one count of a unit (decision 225.a): what the count opens, in a state a person should look at or
one a person decided (`OPENED_BY_A_COUNT`).

TablePreview.title: TablePreview
TablePreview.description:
A correction's text as the table it would be, read by the core's table parser as a reading's table is (204.a);
None where it is no table, or not a clean one.

Trace.title: Trace
Trace.description: Where a reading came from: everything the export records about it except its check.

Unverifiable.title: Unverifiable
Unverifiable.description: A block stage 2 cannot check against the text layer, and why; an older plan gives the why alone.

VerdictForm.title: VerdictForm
VerdictForm.description:
What the page view's dialog offers: whether verdicts are given here at all, and if not why, the lists it chooses
from in the core's own words, and each served knowledge base's export.

VerdictGiven.title: VerdictGiven
VerdictGiven.description: A recorded verdict: its id, the reading it judged, the page's route before it, and the export it set going.

VerdictRequest.title: VerdictRequest
VerdictRequest.description: A verdict on the reading a page shows: the page by its work's id and PDF page, as the views address it.

Work.title: Work
Work.description:
One work as the sources view lists it. A licensed work has no catalog entry: its export gives an id and a title,
the PDF's stem as on the search server, and the catalog's fields stay empty.

WorkReadings.title: WorkReadings
WorkReadings.description: A work's page readings in figures, each value as often as it occurs.
